mustFire.why: the page holds only the last three lines of the verbatim record, which began four pages earlier; the next page is forced
mustFire.construction: pre#verbatim: 97 lines on a fixed 40 px pitch (one display: block span per line). Its page opens with h2.record (48 px + 16 px); lines per page: floor((971.34 - 64) / 40) = 22, then floor(971.34 / 40) = 24, 24, 24, leaving 97 - 94 = 3 lines (120 px) for the tail page. The appendix heading after it has break-before: page. Net fill of the tail page is about 3 x 18.6 px / 971 px = 0.06 against 0.5.
mustFire.docsBasis: docs/rules/layout-orphaned-continuation-page.md; the incoming break of the tail page is an overflow.

mustNotFire.why: middle pages of the record: completely full (24 lines each) and the record continues onto the next page, so they hold the middle of a block, not its tail. At 12 pt monospace on a 40 px pitch the glyph bands cover about 0.46 of the page (G-15 class), which is below the 0.5 threshold; a tool that judges them by net fill alone reports a full page.
mustNotFire.docsBasis: docs/rules/layout-orphaned-continuation-page.md: 'A page holds nothing but the tail of a block that began earlier.'

dependsOn.status: rule page and rule change pending in this release
dependsOn.semantics: a page is judged only where its content ends: its last flow block is the final fragment of its block, or the next page opens with a fresh block
dependsOn.basis: The rule page at the base commit judges every continuation-only page by net fill alone, and these pages read about 0.46-0.47 against 0.50, so under the base wording they would fire. The release changes the rule and its page (WP-F4); the new page states that a page is judged only "where its content ends". This entry holds under that sentence. A gate reports it as 'depends on G-15 semantics' and treats a failure before that sentence is on the rule page as the known state, not as a new false alarm.
